newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends session 1.55 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends session 1.55 pct lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange on Thursday dropped 1.55 percent in a move seen as a correction after weeks of mainly heading up, fuelled by what are seen as some artificially high share prices, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 679.08 points from 689.75 points on Wednesday.

"The bourse index showed a significant drop today of 1.55 percent interpreted as a slight correction compared with the previous weeks' surge...After reaching a peak, the prices are gradually going down to comply with the market's real growth," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of market blue chips, lost 59 dirhams to close at 629 dirhams, a trader said.

The bank, which has a market capitalisation of more than 9.6 billion dirhams, recently allowed the German Commerzbank to increase its stake in BMCE to 10 percent from 1.6 percent, worth $100 million at the current market price.
Samir, Morocco's main refinery, also lost 21 dirhams to close at 336.10 dirhams.

Samir, which has a market capitalisation of more than 6.0 billion dirhams, is expected to cede up to 51 percent of its capital to strategic investors soon, a broker said. The refinery floated one-third of its capital on the bourse last year.

ONA Group, the country's largest private conglomerate, remained stable at 840 dirhams. Its subsidiaries Cosumar sugar refinery and Financiere Diwan, lost 15 dirhams and 10 dirhams respectively, to close at 1,100 dirhams and 356 dirhams over the previous session.
But its third listed subsidiary Centrale Laitiere, one of its high profit makers, jumped 166 dirhams to close at 2,966 dirhams.

Privatisation bonds known as BDP1 and BDP2, which were introduced in 1996 on the bourse as instruments for the purchase of privatised firms, were traded respectively at 1,442 and 1,215 dirhams or up 17 dirhams and 10 dirhams per bond.
Total traded volume rose to more than 160.8 million dirhams from 126 million dirhams on Wednesday.

It was divided into 79.26 million dirhams in shares and 5.49 million dirhams in privatisation bonds traded on the official market. The remaining 76.06 million dirhams were traded in shares on the over the counter market, officials said.
